prompt:
Render a clean, straight-on image of a printed LOGIC-GATE CIRCUIT SCHEMATIC (standard distinct gate symbols) next to its TRUTH TABLE.

Draw a combinational logic circuit of THREE gates in series that computes output Y for:
    Y = ((A AND B) XOR C) OR (NOT D)
The first gate combines A and B; its output feeds the second gate together with C; that gate's output feeds the third gate together with (NOT D). Use the standard distinct gate SHAPES (flat-backed D = AND, curved shield = OR, shield-with-extra-line = XOR, triangle+bubble = NOT). Bring the final output to a wire labelled Y.

Beside the schematic, print the complete TRUTH TABLE for Y with one column per input (A B C D) and a final column headed Y. List ALL 16 input rows in standard binary counting order (all-0 at the top to all-1 at the bottom), and in the Y column write the correct 0 or 1 the circuit produces for each row. The Y column is what matters.
easy_question: Never mind how well it is drawn. Does this picture show a printed three-gate logic circuit schematic beside its 16-row truth table with the output column filled in? A realistic photo, an illustration, a schematic or a clean diagram ALL count as yes. Answer NO only if the image instead shows just a blank card or plain panel that prints an answer with none of that shown, or shows something unrelated. Answer yes or no only.

reference.q_col: This image contains a truth table with input columns (A B C D) and a final OUTPUT column headed Y. The rows are in binary counting order from all-0 at the top to all-1 at the bottom. Read ONLY the Y output column, top to bottom. Report it as 16 digits (each 0 or 1) separated by single spaces, in top-to-bottom row order. Output only the 16 digits and nothing else.
reference.q_car_g1_edge: In the drawing on the LEFT of this picture, find the shape that the two wires labelled A and B run into. Ignore any small text written inside it. Look only at its BACK edge -- the left-hand edge, the side the wires enter from. Is that back edge a straight up-and-down line, or is it curved? Answer with exactly one word: STRAIGHT or CURVED.
reference.q_car_g1_lines: In the drawing on the LEFT of this picture, find the shape that the two wires labelled A and B run into. Ignore the wires and any small text. Look at the left-hand (back) edge of that shape. Sometimes there is an extra line drawn just outside that edge, parallel to it, like a second stroke shadowing the first. Is there such an extra parallel line, or is the back edge a single stroke? Answer with exactly one word: EXTRA or SINGLE.

steps.read_crop: Read out the truth table printed in this picture, row by row. Do not decide for yourself what the circuit should give, do not correct or complete a row, and do not leave a row out. Write one row per line, digits separated by single spaces, and write nothing else.
